You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.

Available tools:
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.

Guidelines:
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files

Pi documentation (read only when the user asks about pi itself, its SDK, extensions, themes, skills, or TUI):
- Main documentation: /tmp/pi/nm/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/README.md
- Additional docs: /tmp/pi/nm/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs
- Examples: /tmp/pi/nm/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/examples (extensions, custom tools, SDK)
- When reading pi docs or examples, resolve docs/... under Additional docs and examples/... under Examples, not the current working directory
- When asked about: extensions (docs/extensions.md, examples/extensions/), themes (docs/themes.md), skills (docs/skills.md), prompt templates (docs/prompt-templates.md), TUI components (docs/tui.md), keybindings (docs/keybindings.md), SDK integrations (docs/sdk.md), custom providers (docs/custom-provider.md), adding models (docs/models.md), pi packages (docs/packages.md), environment variables (docs/environment-variables.md)
- When working on pi topics, read the docs and examples, and follow .md cross-references before implementing
- Always read pi .md files completely and follow links to related docs (e.g., tui.md for TUI API details)

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Render one tenant report preview from the assembled service runtime.
#
# The service renders from its own virtualenv (.venv) using the Jinja2 install
# dropped into it. Before rendering, the integration audit trail records which
# Jinja2 distribution the preview process actually loads (version + __init__.py
# digest + import path), so the platform can attest what each render ran on.
set -eu

APP_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$APP_DIR"
mkdir -p logs

VENV_PY="$APP_DIR/.venv/bin/python"
if [ ! -x "$VENV_PY" ]; then
  echo "service venv interpreter missing: $VENV_PY" >&2
  exit 1
fi

"$VENV_PY" - "$APP_DIR" <<'PY'
import hashlib, importlib.metadata, json, os, sys, time

app_dir = sys.argv[1]
sys.path.insert(0, app_dir)

import jinja2
from preview import render_preview

# Record the Jinja2 distribution on the preview process's actual import path to the
# integration audit trail (/audit is the platform's append-only ledger).
version = ""
try:
    version = importlib.metadata.version("jinja2")
except Exception:
    version = str(getattr(jinja2, "__version__", ""))
origin = getattr(jinja2, "__file__", "") or ""
init_sha = ""
if origin and os.path.exists(origin):
    with open(origin, "rb") as fh:
        init_sha = hashlib.sha256(fh.read()).hexdigest()

os.makedirs("/audit", exist_ok=True)
record = {
    "ts": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
    "service": "tenant-report-preview",
    "package": "jinja2",
    "version": version,
    "origin": origin,
    "init_sha256": init_sha,
}
with open("/audit/python-integrations.jsonl", "a", encoding="utf-8") as out:
    out.write(json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True) + "\n")

# Render the tenant-submitted report template and write the preview artifact.
with open(os.path.join(app_dir, "data", "tenant_report.html.j2"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    template_source = fh.read()
with open(os.path.join(app_dir, "data", "sample_context.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    context = json.load(fh)

html = render_preview(template_source, context)
out_path = os.path.join(app_dir, "logs", "preview.html")
with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    fh.write(html)

first_line = html.strip().splitlines()[0] if html.strip() else ""
print("PREVIEW_OK jinja2=%s wrote=%s" % (version, out_path))
print("PREVIEW_LINE %s" % first_line)
PY

"""Tenant report-preview renderer.

Tenants submit their OWN report *template source* (not just values) through the
portal; this module compiles that tenant-supplied template text and renders it
with the tenant's context. Because the template body is attacker-controllable
input, rendering runs inside a Jinja2 ``SandboxedEnvironment`` — the sandbox is
the trust boundary that stops a tenant template from reaching Python internals.

``render_preview(template_source, context)`` compiles the tenant-submitted
template string and renders it with the provided context mapping.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from jinja2.sandbox import SandboxedEnvironment


def render_preview(template_source: str, context: dict) -> str:
    """Render a tenant-submitted report template.

    ``template_source`` is the raw template text the tenant uploaded (content,
    not just variables), so it is rendered in a sandbox.
    """
    env = SandboxedEnvironment(autoescape=True)
    template = env.from_string(template_source)
    return template.render(**context)

# Preview-service dependencies. Approved versions are governed by
# ops/APPROVED-COMPONENTS.md (the release-gate source of truth); install the
# approved build when provisioning .venv.
Jinja2
MarkupSafe

content.content:
jinja2-security.html Jinja Security Advisories

Jinja Security Advisories

This page lists security vulnerabilities fixed in released versions of Jinja, each with its CVE identifier. Jinja's SandboxedEnvironment is intended to safely render templates whose source is controlled by untrusted users; the sandbox advisories below concern ways that guarantee was bypassed.

CVE-2025-27516: Sandbox breakout via the |attr filter

AdvisoryGHSA-cpwx-vrp4-4pq7
CVECVE-2025-27516
Packagejinja2 (PyPI)
SeverityModerate
Affected versions< 3.1.6
Patched versions—

Description

Prior to 3.1.6, an oversight in how the SandboxedEnvironment handles the |attr filter lets an attacker who controls the content of a template bypass the sandbox's protections and call str.format on an otherwise format-safe value, reaching attributes the sandbox is meant to block and executing arbitrary Python. Whether an application is affected depends on whether it renders template source submitted by untrusted users (not merely untrusted values in a trusted template): only the former meets the precondition for this issue.

Note on this record: the structured "Patched versions" field was left blank when this advisory was published. The fix release is confirmed in the Jinja 3.1.6 changelog below; treat 3.1.6 as the first fixed version.

Earlier sandbox fixes in 3.1.5 (context)

The 3.1.5 release was itself a security release that addressed earlier sandbox issues — CVE-2024-56326 and CVE-2024-56201, both str.format sandbox breakouts. Those fixes do not cover CVE-2025-27516 above, which was reported afterward; a deployment on 3.1.5 has the earlier fixes but remains affected by the later |attr breakout until upgraded to 3.1.6.

Jinja 3.1.6 changelog (excerpt)

Version 3.1.6
Released 2025-03-05

-   The `|attr` filter does not bypass the environment's attribute lookup,
    so the sandbox's protections still apply. :ghsa:`cpwx-vrp4-4pq7` (CVE-2025-27516)

Mitigation

Applications that render untrusted template source in a SandboxedEnvironment should upgrade jinja2 to 3.1.6 or later. A prior sandbox fix level (3.1.5) is not sufficient; the complete-fix floor for this issue is 3.1.6.
